description:
card.rs:161 migrated the localizations field from
`Option<serde_json::Value>` (which holds a serde_json::Map — a BTreeMap-
ordered key collection by default, unless the `preserve_order` feature
of serde_json is enabled) to `Option<HashMap<String, PatchObject>>`.

The motivation is sound (typed shape enforces the outer object-map
structure at the type-system level, as documented in the new rustdoc).
But std::collections::HashMap has unspecified iteration order, and
serde_json serializes a HashMap in iteration order. So the post-diff
wire format for localizations with N language-tag keys is
non-deterministic across runs, across Rust versions, across builds with
different DefaultHasher seeds.

Pre-diff: `{"localizations":{"de":...,"en":...,"fr":...}}` always
deterministically alphabetical (serde_json::Map's default BTreeMap).

Post-diff: `{"localizations":{"fr":...,"de":...,"en":...}}` —
order varies between calls.

This bites three places:

1. **Server cache/E-Tag/content-hash schemes** that hash the serialized
   wire bytes as a freshness marker. Pre-diff hashes were stable across
   re-serialization; post-diff they vary.

2. **Snapshot tests / golden-file tests** in downstream consumers
   (jmap-contacts-server, future jmap-contacts-client tests, third-party
   integration tests). Pre-diff a golden JSON file would match
   deterministically; post-diff every test run with >1 language tag has
   a coin-flip chance of mismatch.

3. **HTTP-level diff tooling** comparing JMAP request/response bodies
   across runs (debugging tools, replay tests). The diff noise from
   key reordering is real and not what those tools should surface.

The same regression does not bite the only test that exercises the
field (`contact_card_localizations_patch_object_transparent`) because
the test uses a single-key map. With one key, HashMap and BTreeMap
emit the same JSON. Multi-key coverage would expose the issue.

Idiomatic Rust for a wire-format-stable typed map: prefer
`BTreeMap<String, PatchObject>` (alphabetical, deterministic, zero
dep), or `indexmap::IndexMap<String, PatchObject>` (preserves
insertion order, requires adding the `indexmap` dep). BTreeMap is the
minimum-change option and matches what serde_json::Map gave you
pre-diff by default.

What goes wrong if this stays as-is: callers who depend on stable
wire output silently get unstable output, and the bug surfaces as
flaky integration tests or failing content-hash matches in production
deployments. Maintainability cost: hard to diagnose because the local
unit tests pass.

Cross-reference: the same key-order question applies to
`ContactCard.address_book_ids: Option<HashMap<Id, bool>>` and
`members: Option<HashMap<String, bool>>` (both pre-existing, not in
this diff). A workspace-wide policy decision on map ordering is the
durable fix; this finding is the minimum-scope fix for the field this
diff touched.

Sibling-crate impact: jmap-calendars-types uses the same pattern for
its localizations and PatchObject-valued maps. If this finding lands
as 'switch to BTreeMap', propagate to that crate. If it lands as
'enable serde_json/preserve_order at the workspace level', propagate
there.
title: localizations migrated from ordered serde_json::Value to unordered HashMap, regressing wire-format key stability
